solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heavy drinker blushes, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says only part of the word blushes is wanted, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A drinker reddens a little, perhaps from embarrassment or the drink itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush is informal slang, mostly American, for a habitual drunkard.

clue.text: Cricket ball causing fracture?

parts.note: read literally, a ball that injures a limb; in cricket it is a spin delivery turning from the leg side

explanation.surface: A fast delivery in cricket hits a batsman hard enough to break a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a leg-break is a delivery from a spin bowler that turns from the leg side towards the off side; the question mark flags the literal broken-leg reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket term for a spinning delivery doubles, taken literally, as a fractured limb.

clue.text: Small enthusiastic group of workers

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a warm welcome is an enthusiastic one

explanation.surface: A little band of keen employees, perhaps a committed team at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The workers are worker bees, not office staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster of bees on the move is the classic collective noun for the insects that labour in a hive.

clue.text: One who values beasts of burden? So right

parts.note: asses, or donkeys, are classic pack animals

explanation.surface: A valuer of donkeys is asked to confirm that is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor is an official who estimates the worth of property, often for tax or insurance.

clue.text: Sports team breaking up? Very funny

parts.note: a side is a team, as in a football side
splitting means breaking apart

explanation.surface: A club side falling apart is described, oddly, as hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hilarious enough to make your sides ache with laughter is described with this idiom.

clue.text: The King distributed silver no end

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no end says the last letter of the word silver is dropped

explanation.surface: A monarch hands out silver until none is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' drops the R of silver, leaving SILVE, which 'distributed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was nicknamed the King of Rock and Roll, often just the King.

clue.text: Wise man taking flight alone on Monday

parts.note: a pilot's solo is a flight made without anyone else

explanation.surface: A sage sets off on a lone journey at the start of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon of the Bible is proverbial for his wisdom.

clue.text: Almost prepared to study

indicators.note: almost says the word is not quite complete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: ready means prepared

explanation.surface: Someone is nearly ready to start revising.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a subject at university is to read it, a British usage, as in reading law.

clue.text: Correct homework again, and make comment

definitions.meaning: to mark a pupil's work a second time
to say something by way of observation

explanation.surface: A teacher regrades the homework and adds remarks in the margin.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits as RE- (again) plus MARK (correct homework).
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: marking again, and passing an observation aloud or in writing.

clue.text: Enterprising leader of Indian state?

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast
a head is a leader, as of a school or company

explanation.surface: A question about what makes a good chief minister in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of Indian state' is the head of Goa, written GOA then HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead person or firm is ambitious and ready to try new ventures.

clue.text: Holiday property unfavourably situated in Virginia

indicators.note: situated in says the word for badly is placed within the state's abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
ill means badly or unfavourably, as in ill-advised

explanation.surface: A holiday home in Virginia is in a poor location.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a detached house rented out to holidaymakers, especially around the Mediterranean.

clue.text: After drink, bachelor wants a dance

indicators.note: after says the bachelor's letter follows the spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a kind of drink
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: Having had a drink, a single man wants to get up and dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Opening seed?

parts.note: the magic words 'open' plus this seed opened the robbers' cave in Ali Baba

explanation.walkthrough: In the Ali Baba tale, the password that opens the thieves' cave is 'Open' followed by the name of this seed, so it is a seed that opens things.
explanation.definitionFit: The small oily seed used on bread rolls is also the password in the Arabian Nights tale.

clue.text: Doctor eats head of terribly large fish

indicators.note: eats says the doctor takes another letter inside him

parts.note: a surgeon is a kind of doctor

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word terribly

explanation.surface: A physician is consuming something enormous and fishy, terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' puts T, the head of 'terribly', inside SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a huge river and sea fish, the source of caviar.

clue.text: Tossed about on Italy's lakes, probably

indicators.note: something tossed about is thrown around, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boat is pitched about on the Italian lakes, quite likely.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means there is an even chance or better, much like the plain adverb.

clue.text: Country lake overlooking Spain and Portugal

indicators.note: overlooking in a down clue puts the lake's letter above the peninsula

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
Iberia is the peninsula shared by Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A lake with a view across the Iberian peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African nation founded by freed American slaves.

clue.text: A woman from America in another country

parts.note: broad is dated American slang for a woman

explanation.surface: An American woman is living overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abroad is to be overseas, away from home.

clue.text: Miserable sailor about to board plane

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common crossword sailor

indicators.note: to board means to get onto, so the letter goes inside the plane

parts.note: a jet is a plane
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: An unhappy seaman is just about to get on his flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject means wretched or hopeless, as in abject poverty.

clue.text: English before ten in the morning, then first of science tests

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
a.m. marks a time before noon

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the word science

explanation.surface: A school timetable: English first thing at ten, followed by science papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are formal written tests of a student's knowledge.

clue.text: I received your message, man

definitions.meaning: radio jargon acknowledging that a transmission has been heard and understood

explanation.surface: A radio operator acknowledges a call and addresses the other fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio acknowledgement comes from the old phonetic alphabet's word for R, received; it is also a man's name.

clue.text: Formidable sounding tale-teller

indicators.note: sounding says the word for formidable is heard, not spelt as such

parts.note: grim means forbidding or formidable

explanation.surface: A storyteller whose voice is fearsome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brothers Grimm collected and published German folk tales such as Hansel and Gretel.

clue.text: Work available in shop usually

indicators.note: available in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A product is generally on sale at the store.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for a work, especially a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: Father and mother run inside Italian city

indicators.note: inside says the run's letter is placed within the parents' words

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
ma is an informal word for mother
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A couple of parents dash about indoors, in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Parma is a northern Italian city famous for its ham and cheese.

clue.text: Silver found during one excavation? Fancy!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: found during says the metal lies within the dig

parts.note: a mine is a dug-out working
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone digging strikes silver and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise: fancy that, just picture it.

clue.text: Maybe Leo has prominent role, singing regularly

parts.note: a performer who stars has the lead role

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word singing is taken

explanation.surface: A performer called Leo takes the lead and sings at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks Leo as one example; 'regularly' takes I, G, N from 'singing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve zodiac signs in astrology.

clue.text: Change of name? I'll second that

indicators.note: change of says the letters of the word name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone backs a proposal to rename something.
explanation.definitionFit: Said at the close of a prayer, the word expresses agreement, so it serves as 'hear, hear'.
